hook_text: This purple juice from red cabbage can tell lemon juice from soap. Watch the colours.
clip_script: Acids and bases mostly look like plain water, and tasting them is never allowed. So chemists use colour spies called indicators. Litmus is the classic: acid turns blue litmus red, base turns red litmus blue. Universal indicator is a mix of spies that makes a rainbow: red for strong acid, orange, yellow, green at neutral 7, blue, and purple for strong base. But you can make your own. Chop red cabbage, soak it in hot water, and pour off the purple juice. Drip it into lemon juice: pink. Into water: purple. Into bicarbonate of soda: blue-green. Into washing soda: green. Same juice, different colours, all because of pH. Even the turmeric in curry is a spy, which is why a curry stain on a white shirt turns red in soapy wash water.
visual_style: A row of glasses changing colour as purple cabbage juice is poured in; litmus strips flipping colour; a universal indicator chart sliding across the screen.
pacing: Quick setup, then a rhythmic pour-and-reveal sequence, ending on the curry stain.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make your own cabbage indicator at home.
